name: Matrimony.com Ltd
title: Matrimony.com Ltd - 540704 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Matchmaking revenue up 17.9% YoY with paid subs +26.6% but ATV down 12.2%; management guides Q3 billing single-digit, PAT Rs19-20 crore, and Q2 PAT growth of 167% met the triple-digit prior guide.

triggers.quote: Added 3.02 lakh paid subscription during the quarter, which is a growth of 26.6% year-on-year

triggers.label: Q3 billing single-digit growth guided
triggers.quote: Matchmaking billing are expected to reach a single-digit year-on-year growth in quarter three

summary.headline: Matrimony.com Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.6% YoY to INR134.8 crore, with EBITDA up 144.7% to INR30.3 crore and PAT up 167.3% to INR20.7 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated billing grew 10.7% YoY to INR131.1 crore but fell 3.6% QoQ, while revenue grew 17.6% YoY to INR134.8 crore. Matchmaking paid subscriptions rose 26.6% YoY to 3.02 lakh, while ATV fell 12.2% YoY as shorter one-month packages were offered to selected user cohorts. Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 22.5% from 10.8% a year ago, helped by lower marketing spend relative to revenue. Management guided Q3 revenue to double-digit YoY growth but billing to only single-digit growth, citing Shradh and Navratri timing, and PAT to triple-digit YoY growth at a level similar to Q1 or slightly below Q2.

financial_highlights.change: vs 20.1% in Q1 FY27 and 10.8% a year ago
vs 26.9% in Q1 FY27 and 17.1% a year ago

segments.name: Matchmaking
segments.commentary: Revenue INR133.9 crore (+17.9% YoY); billing INR130.3 crore (+10.9% YoY). Added 3.02 lakh paid subscriptions (+26.6% YoY, +11.2% QoQ), ATV down 12.2% YoY and 13.3% QoQ. Marketing spend INR45.3 crore vs INR46.5 crore in Q1.

segments.name: Marriage Services and Other
segments.commentary: Billing INR79 lakh (+7% QoQ, -15.5% YoY); revenue INR89 lakh (-7% QoQ, -14.7% YoY). EBITDA loss INR4.3 crore vs INR3.8 crore in Q1 FY27 and INR2.8 crore in Q2 FY26.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 Matchmaking revenue expected to grow double digits YoY; Matchmaking billing expected to grow single digits YoY due to Shradh and Navratri falling in Q3 this year versus Q2 last year.
Q3 PAT expected to grow triple digits YoY, at a level similar to Q1 or slightly below Q2 FY27; a call answer cited INR19-20 crore range.
Marketing spend for Matchmaking expected to stay at a similar level, with no substantial increase planned; management said it could slightly decline.
Marriage Services and Other billing expected to be higher than Q2 in Q3.
For FY27, revenue growth expected to be double digit, with Q4 expected to bounce back.
Non-matchmaking revenue aspiration of triple-digit growth next year (FY28), per management in response to an analyst question.
capex_capacity: Paid subscriptions at about 3 lakh per quarter, with management saying this volume level is sustainable helped by the shorter one-month package.

Proposed acquisition of an additional 50% stake in Astro-Vision Futuretech Private Limited, approved by the Board, subject to closing conditions and regulatory approvals; Astro-Vision has annual revenue of about INR18-20 crore and EBITDA break-even to minor losses of INR1-2 crore (as stated on the call). Share of Astro-Vision Q2 loss was INR21 lakh.
Wedding Services moved from vendor subscription to a commission-based model; WedAssist operates only in Tamil Nadu for now, with other markets to follow after scale and success metrics are met.
Regional Luv.com brands launched in the quarter: Premam (Kerala), Priyam (Tamil Nadu), Premalu (Andhra Pradesh); further regional languages planned in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Matchmaking ATV down 12.2% YoY and 13.3% QoQ, as a one-month package was introduced for selected cohorts; management said it is not discounting and that conversion rose (rate not disclosed).
Management says the shorter-duration package adds volume without cutting revenue from longer-duration paying users, though some overlap exists.
Paid users rose to about 5.7 lakh in H1 FY27 per management, versus about 5 lakh in Q1 and Q2 combined from a prior comparison; management cited a 70,000 increase.
Competition: management said competitive intensity has eased in North and some other markets; the company is a strong player in South, West and East, and is a leader but not number one in North.

Aadhaar-based verification approved by the Government of India for voluntary member verification; management says it is the only matrimony company with such approval, with launch planned in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: With paid users up about 26-27% but ATV down about 11%, how is revenue per user protected from cheaper plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-month package is targeted at specific cohorts based on spending capacity, aimed at conversion, with some overlap but net benefit; it is not discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Can 22% margins be protected if marketing rises and Astro-Vision investment is made?
qa_highlights.answer: Matchmaking marketing expected at a similar level with no substantial increase; Astro-Vision (about INR20 crore annualised business) is expected to be integrated with the user base and not to hurt margins.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term revenue growth outlook given falling ATV: single-digit or double-digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 revenue growth will be double digit in Q3 and Q4; Q3 billing single-digit is timing-driven by festivals, and Q4 will catch up.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q3 billing guided to single digit and can Q2-level profit be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Shradh and Navratri fall in Q3 this year versus Q2 last year; management expects Q3 PAT similar to H1 levels, with expenses at a similar level.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a special dividend or larger buyback given cash of over INR200-300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board will decide on rewarding shareholders; the one-year buyback cooling-off period ends next year and the Board will decide then.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Marriage Services keep making losses and when will it be shut or scaled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is not closing it; the model moved from vendor subscriptions to commission-based wedding services, with the team and product costs being built and growth expected quarter on quarter.

risks_watch: Continued ATV decline (down 12.2% YoY) if the one-month package dilutes revenue per user; monitor ATV and paid volume together.
Q3 billing guided to single-digit YoY growth, with festival timing affecting the quarter; Q4 catch-up needs to materialise.
Marriage Services and Other still loss-making (EBITDA loss INR4.3 crore in Q2), with a model change still early and only in Tamil Nadu.
Astro-Vision acquisition (additional 50%) subject to closing conditions and approvals; cash deployment and synergy case not quantified.
Competitive intensity in North markets, where the company is not number one; management said any increase in marketing there would not materially affect growth or margins.
CFO appointment not yet finalised, as stated on the call.
Management did not disclose conversion rates or paid-user churn figures; the Matchmaking margin gain relies heavily on lower marketing intensity.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, paid volume and the Q3 profit outlook, but guarded on specifics: conversion rates, market share and buyback or special dividend plans were not quantified. Management was evasive on the Marriage Services losses and on the exact Astro-Vision economics.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report a strong performance during the quarter with growth across our key financial parameters.
At this point, we are the only matrimony company approved by the Government of India to get the Aadhaar-based verification of members.
So, there is an increase in volume without affecting the revenue contribution from the key customer base.
We do not see anything is going to change in this market.

adds.what: Astro-Vision Futuretech additional 50% stake acquisition (not organic capacity; Board-approved, subject to closing and regulatory approvals)
Regional Luv.com brands (Premam, Priyam, Premalu) launched; further regional languages planned

growth.why: Management guides Q3 Matchmaking revenue to double-digit YoY growth but billing only single-digit (Shradh/Navratri timing), FY27 revenue double-digit growth with Q4 bounce, backed by paid subscriptions up 26.6% YoY and lower marketing spend rather than capacity; no numeric capacity additions, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 22.5% from 20.1% in Q1 and 10.8% a year ago, with Matchmaking margin at 29.7%, and marketing expected flat to slightly lower while Q3 PAT is guided at INR19-20 crore, similar to Q1 or slightly below Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity additions were discussed; growth is from paid subscriptions (3.02 lakh, +26.6% YoY) and a shorter one-month package, not new plants or lines.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Paid subscriptions rose 26.6% YoY to 3.02 lakh and management calls about 3 lakh per quarter sustainable, though Q3 matchmaking billing is guided to only single-digit YoY growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex intensity is minimal and no capex plan was disclosed; the only inorganic move is the Board-approved additional 50% stake in Astro-Vision, which is a stake purchase rather than capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 revenue to double-digit growth with a Q4 bounce, and Q3 matchmaking revenue to double-digit YoY, but gave no numeric upgrade and ATV is falling 12.2% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 matchmaking billing is guided to single-digit YoY growth, and ATV is down 12.2% YoY, so the Q4 catch-up needs to materialise or FY27 double-digit growth is at risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Regional Luv.com brands Premam, Priyam and Premalu launched this quarter with further regional languages planned, and Aadhaar-based verification launch was planned in the quarter.

rows.label: ATV dilution from one-month package
rows.why: Matchmaking ATV fell 12.2% YoY and 13.3% QoQ as a one-month package was introduced for selected cohorts; management says it is not discounting and conversion rose, but the conversion rate was not disclosed.

rows.label: Marriage Services model shift to commission
rows.why: The segment still lost INR4.3 crore EBITDA in Q2 (vs INR3.8 crore in Q1), and the WedAssist commission model is live only in Tamil Nadu with other markets to follow after scale metrics are met.

rows.label: Shareholder return or buyback decision
rows.why: Cash is about INR345 crore, but management said the Board will decide on rewarding shareholders and the buyback cooling-off ends next year.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, paid volume and the Q3 PAT outlook, but guarded on conversion rates, buyback plans and Marriage Services losses; analysts pressed on falling ATV, Q3 single-digit billing and why the loss-making segment is not being closed.

oneOffs.what: Matchmaking paid subscriptions +26.6% YoY to 3.02 lakh added, offset by ATV -12.2% YoY from shorter one-month package; revenue growth is volume-driven with lower revenue per user
EBITDA margin expansion (to 22.5% from 10.8% a year ago) relies on lower marketing intensity, not disclosed as one-off but not recurring-proven

quality.why: Revenue grew 17.6% YoY on paid-subscription volume (+26.6%) while ATV fell 12.2%, and billing grew only 10.7%, so the headline revenue growth runs ahead of billing; no discrete one-off gain or low base is disclosed, but the revenue-to-billing gap and marketing-driven margin gain are not clearly recurring.
